key_points: The +14% move on Nov 23 was a sector-wide rebound tied to Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, not LRCX-specific news, and premarket weakness on Nov 24 already gives some back — low durability.

Fundamentals remain intact: record September-quarter revenue of $8.22B, strong profitability and a positive outlook on AI-driven equipment demand, but this is already reported/known and largely priced.
China at ~35% of sales is a persistent structural risk for export-control headlines.
Stock still ~54% below its June high after the AI selloff, so positioning/valuation is more supportive than a year ago, but no fresh catalyst to re-rate near term.
Remaining headlines are options-quote noise, peer commentary (Micron DRAM, KLA Singapore) and generic AI-bubble commentary — no thesis change.
